newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Bid for NZ's Transmark shrs to go ahead at NZ$1.60.
newsitem.headline: Bid for NZ's Transmark shrs to go ahead at NZ$1.60.

text.p: Gandava Investments Ltd's NZ$1.60 a share takeover bid for Transmark Corp Ltd will proceed despite the offer falling well short of an independent valuation, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Thursday.
Ernst and Young put the bid in doubt when it found fair value for the electronics distributor to be between $2.00 and $2.15.
Undeterred, Transmark managing director Nico Wamsteker, who is part of the takeover attempt, confirmed yesterday that the bid would go ahead.
The offer would be made to shareholders on Friday.
Placing a price earnings ratio on the company of 10.94 was too high, he said.
Ernst and Young had compared Transmark with companies like Ebos and Steel and Tube in arriving at that ratio, but it was not in the same league, Wamsteker said.
"Our bid is at a ratio of 8.4, which is a very generous price for the company on forecast earnings."
The valuation was based on Transmark reporting a profit of around $2.9 million for the year to December 31, excluding the sale of its U-Bix holding.
In the past six months, 75 percent of the shares traded in Transmark have been bought by the Hong Kong based Shriro Group, which has a 74.05 percent stake. These were brought at $1.45 each, he said.
Shriro is the major partner in the takeover Vehicle, Gandava Investments. Wamsteker, who has a 6.21 percent holding in Transmark, also has an interest in Gandava.
